steps.content: Once the attack begins, it will be too late. You must find her immediately.
To avoid raising any alarms, you calmly walk straight to your room.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The switch for the secret passage should be right around... here.
[Secret Passage]
The walls within are coated in ghostly fluorescent paint. You drop to a crouch—the floor is bare. No footprints.
They know about the passage, but they haven't come through. You've beaten them here.
There's still time.
[Hilda's Study]

Inside, heavy velvet curtains mute the unrelenting storm and the chaos down in the hall, creating an island of tense silence. Hilda is hunched over her desk, her entire focus locked on the Monolith prototype.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Do you need something, ${PlayerName}?

steps.speaker: Option
options: There's going to be a real attack.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I just got word. There's an attack coming in twenty minutes. I think all the guards are in on it. Their plan is to storm the manor, kill everyone, and take the Monolith. We need to get ready. Now.
She doesn't immediately accept your story, but she doesn't reject it out of hand either.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: What's your source?
You cross the room to Hilda's wardrobe, fling the doors open, and with a few practiced motions, pry away the false back panel.
A yawning, pitch-black passage is revealed. Within the darkness, a series of faint, fluorescent marks hover in the air. When you look at Hilda, her face is a mask of shock.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Did you just say... the guards?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Think about it. If you could use them to stage a fake attack, why couldn't the mole use them to launch a real one?
The light catches half her face, revealing a stern profile. The faint smile is gone, her lips now a tight, severe line.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: How much do you know?
You take a deep breath and reveal what you've discovered.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The "attack" used non-lethal rounds. They deliberately avoided any angles that could cause real casualties. With that much gunfire, we didn't have a single injury? And it was just... "subdued." That's not believable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It was more like an elaborate fireworks show. Designed to create the illusion of chaos.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Looking back now, certain details seem a little too convenient.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You knew Johnson had connections with a few here, so you loosened security around him to draw the mole out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But you never expected it would involve innocent people. That it would lead to real casualties.
Finally, Hilda turns to you. Her movement is deliberate, unhurried. When her eyes meet yours, there is not a trace of hesitation in her gaze.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Johnson's death was necessary. His actions alone warranted execution a hundred times over. He was the most obvious, weakest link in the mole's network. His stupidity and fear were a liability.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I just made use of his corpse. It was an efficient way to flush out potential traitors. Nothing more.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that so? But I don't think that's who you are.
As you speak, you produce the roll of cipher paper, flashing it in her direction before placing it down on the table.

A flicker of naked panic in Hilda's gaze, swiftly mastered. She assesses you, the evidence, and the stakes in a heartbeat. The pretense is over. Now, she might as well hear you out before resorting to more permanent solutions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You hate manufactured sacrifices. You despise involving civilians. You're loyal to the city-state, but you question its orders. Honestly, I wouldn't be surprised if you'd already altered classified documents given the chance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You have your pride. You only eliminate targets you deem deserving. So admit it, Casey's death was never part of your design. It's a flaw in your otherwise perfect plan.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And I was angry. You knew who I was, and you still kept me in the dark. You used me, just like you used everyone else. If I hadn't been quick on my feet, I could have ended up like Casey.
Seeing her lips tighten involuntarily, you soften your tone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not turning you in. Not now, anyway. I believe that even in a war, we need a line we don't cross. A sense of what's right.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But I will say this: one person can only do so much. If we had worked together from the start, maybe we could have avoided this tragedy.
At this point, her agitation suddenly stills. A calculated silence hangs in the air before she breaks it, her voice now measured and clear.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: To be honest, I never expected you to show up here. And you saw through my scheme far quicker than I projected.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You could have remained silent. Or you could have moved against me in the chaos. Yet, you chose to help me.
Your proposal for an alliance hangs in the air. She meets it not with acceptance, but with a steely, knowing look, seamlessly pivoting to lay out her own shrewd assessment of the situation.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: This shows that despite your anger, you've made the most rational choice: aside from me, you trust no one else here. I remain your only viable ally.
Her words leave you utterly speechless.
She is right. The truth is, she isn't in your power; she's your only reliable ally. Any advantage you seemingly hold is purely theoretical.
In seeing this, both of you have proven yourselves a step ahead of Helene.
Having laid her cards on the table, Hilda extends her hand.
Time has taught you to decipher the subtle language behind her icy composure. And now, in her eyes, you see not just calm assessment and approval, but a faint, genuine glimmer of joy.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Thank you for your honesty... and for your fair judgment.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: You have my word. I will not act unilaterally like that again.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: So, let us table the discussion of my... methods, and your objections to them. For now, we need a plan for the very real attack that is coming.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: That, after all, is the immediate priority.

You scout the passage behind the wardrobe again, calculating that a strike team of three or four will likely use it as a point of entry. Any more than that, and the front door remains their primary breach point.
With quiet efficiency, Hilda arranges a decoy from clothes and pillows before the desk, then directs you to use the furniture as concealment.
You've trusted no one else with this plan; the mole is still out there, and a single leak could be fatal.
And so, time passes quickly.

The expected explosion comes, rocking the annex building. Manphist's flustered shout echoes from below, immediately drowned out by the front door splintering open and the thunderous stampede of combat boots on the stairs—
(Sound effect: gunshots at the door)
Almost in sync with the assault on the door, you hear hurried, chaotic footsteps echoing from the depths of the wardrobe passage. They're here.
The room's door is kicked open with a violent crash. A storm of gunfire erupts instantly, shredding Hilda's decoy into a cloud of fabric and stuffing in a matter of seconds.
As the gunsmoke clears, the soldiers' grim realization dawns—they've been lured into a kill box. But the realization comes a heartbeat too late.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Now!
Hilda's shots are precise, shattering wrists and sending guns clattering to the floor.
Yet, even with their hands broken, the guards charge forward, eyes bloodshot with frenzy. There's no choice left—
The last remaining survivor makes a desperate move, raising his hand to bite down on something hidden in his sleeve.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Stop him! He's got a poison pill! We need him alive!
You summon all your strength and drive a powerful punch into the guard's jaw. His head snaps back, and he drops, unconscious.
You lunge forward, locking your hands around his throat and squeezing until his eyes roll back. He collapses to the floor, out cold.
(Paths converge)
A quick pat-down reveals the poison pill. You pry it from his clothes and toss it aside.
Rapid footsteps approach from outside the door.

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: Heard gunshots! Are you two in one piece?!

steps.speaker: L.L.
steps.content: We're fine. What's happening with the fire outside?

steps.speaker: Marlo
steps.content: No idea, but you're safe, that's what counts. Those guards are all traitorous scum anyway. I'll go kill—
As he speaks, he bends down to retrieve the guns dropped by the two guards.
At this moment, you decide to...

options: Stop him from taking the guns
